description.p: systemd Pilot is a graphical front end for systemctl. Manage the units on this computer, or on remote machines over SSH, from one window.

ul.li: Browse system and user units of every type, with instant search
Start, stop, restart, enable and disable units
Read a unit's status, logs, unit file and properties
Read the system journal, with filters and a custom time range
Create new units from templates
Connect to remote hosts with a password, a private key or your SSH agent

screenshot.caption: Details and logs of a unit

description.p: The journal opens quickly in the AppImage again: in about a second, instead of up to eight.
Every unit type, and a closer look at each unit.

ul.li: List every unit type, not just services, with type and status filters in the sidebar
A Dependencies tab shows what a unit requires, what requires it, and what it starts after or before
Reload units, run a timer's job now, clear a failed state, send signals, and mask or unmask units
Create timer and path units along with their service, and enable and start them in one step
Follow the journal as new entries are logged
On this computer, polkit asks for the password and remembers it for a few minutes
Icons are bundled, so the app looks the same on every desktop

description.p: The journal and the services list now share the main window.

ul.li: Read the journal with filters, common-problem presets, search and a custom time range
System and user services are listed together, with filters in the sidebar
Service details open beside the list, including the log and an editor for the unit file
A failed command is shown with its output, which can be copied

description.p: A complete rewrite for GTK 4 and libadwaita.

ul.li: Local and remote machines in one sidebar, with an adaptive layout
User services work everywhere, including logs and controls
Service details now include logs, the unit file and searchable properties
Remote host keys are verified, and passwords are never placed on a command line
Errors from systemctl are reported instead of being shown as success
Hosts can be removed, and editing a host keeps its saved password
